project.name: Eclipse Ditto
project.description: Eclipse Ditto is a mature IoT framework implementing the 'digital twins' pattern, providing virtual cloud-based representations of real-world physical devices and systems like sensors, connected vehicles, smart grids, and EV charging stations.

considerations: EPL-2.0 is a weak copyleft license (similar to LGPL)
Modifications to Ditto code must be released under EPL-2.0
Larger works using Ditto as a library can be under different licenses
Patent license included with non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free terms
Commercial distribution requires indemnification of other contributors
Source code must be made available when distributed
Patent litigation against the Program terminates patent rights
Secondary licensing option available (e.g., GPLv2+) under specific conditions
recommendations: Suitable for commercial and open-source projects
Can be used as a dependency or service without copyleft obligations on your code
If modifying Ditto core code, modifications must be released under EPL-2.0
Ensure contribution agreement is signed if contributing upstream
Review patent grant clauses if patent concerns exist

thing.description: A generic entity serving as a handle for multiple Features belonging to this Thing. Can model physical devices, virtual devices, transactional entities, master data, or other manageable IoT assets.

constraints.namespace_pattern: starts with a-z or A-Z, may include dots, dashes, underscores, and numbers
constraints.name_constraints: cannot be empty, cannot contain forward slashes, must avoid control characters

policyId.description: References the Policy governing read/write permissions for authenticated subjects at hierarchical levels

definition.description: Optional field linking the Thing to a model description (URL or namespace:name:version)
definition.purpose: Describes Thing capabilities, supports W3C WoT Thing Models
definition.validation: Since v3.6.0, Ditto validates modifications against linked Thing Models

attributes.description: Describe the Thing in more detail, can be of any JSON type
attributes.purpose: Model relatively static properties at the Thing level

features.description: Zero or more Features - the primary mechanism for modeling dynamic capabilities

metadata.description: Optional semantic information attached to attributes and features
metadata.purpose: Provides context without being part of twin's value (timestamps, units, change tracking)
metadata.structure: _metadata object that mirrors the thing's hierarchical structure

thing.builder_pattern: Fluent API with newBuilder() and toBuilder() methods for immutable construction

feature.description: Container for organizing related data and functionality within a Thing. Used to manage all data that can be clustered in an outlined technical context.

formats: HTTP/HTTPS URLs (particularly W3C WoT Thing Models)
definition.validation: Definitions serve as semantic documentation, not enforced constraints (unless WoT validation enabled)

properties.type: arbitrary JSON - can be simple/scalar or complex nested objects

desiredProperties.purpose: Stores desired state, searchable and indexed
desiredProperties.note: Currently treated as persistent storage rather than actively processed

feature.builder_pattern: Fluent API with newBuilder() and toBuilder() methods
feature.wot_integration: Supports W3C Web of Things Thing Models in JSON-LD format

policy.description: Defines fine-grained access control specifying 'who gets permissions on what resources'

entries.description: Map of policy entries defining subjects, resources, and permissions

subjects.expiring_subjects: Automatically remove access after ISO-8601 timestamps with hourly granularity

permissions.note: write does not imply read - both must be granted independently
permissions.hierarchical_flow: Permissions flow downward through nested paths unless explicitly revoked

attributes_vs_properties.attributes: Relatively static Thing-level properties (e.g., manufacturer, location, serial number)
attributes_vs_properties.feature_properties: Frequently-changing dynamic data clustered by technical context (e.g., temperature readings, lamp state)
attributes_vs_properties.desired_properties: Target state for device configuration management

multi_tenant_support.pattern: Different organizations use distinct namespace prefixes (e.g., com.acme vs org.competitor)
multi_tenant_support.filtering: Search and subscriptions can filter by namespace for performance

wot_integration.thing_models: Templates defining interaction contracts (like interfaces in OOP)
wot_integration.validation: Since v3.6.0, validates modifications against linked Thing Models
wot_integration.skeleton_generation: Auto-generates initial JSON structures from Thing Model definitions
wot_integration.td_generation: Generates W3C Thing Descriptions from referenced Thing Models

metadata_usage.audit_trails: Track changes with timestamps and user information
metadata_usage.data_semantics: Store unit information or property descriptions
metadata_usage.change_history: Record modification context without altering primary values

twin_channel.characteristics: Always available, eventually consistent with physical device

device_to_twin.mapping: Payload mapping transforms external formats to Ditto Protocol
device_to_twin.enforcement: Source enforcement validates device identity against thing IDs
device_to_twin.qos: Acknowledgements enable QoS 1 'at least once' delivery

twin_to_device.mechanism: Connectivity targets publish events to external systems

merge_operations.behavior: Targeted updates without replacing entire resource
merge_operations.auto_create: Automatically creates Thing if doesn't exist during merge

conditional_updates.path_specific: v3.8.0+ supports different conditions for different merge patch sections

consistency_model.guarantees: search-persisted acknowledgement for guaranteed awareness of persistence

correlation_and_tracking.correlation_id: Each Protocol message contains correlation-id for associating related messages
correlation_and_tracking.response_validation: Ditto ensures responses match correlation ID, entity ID, and path
correlation_and_tracking.event_correlation: Twin events carry correlation IDs of commands that produced them

signals_architecture.concept: Unified communication primitive combining commands, responses, events, and announcements

commands.characteristics: May be refused, not guaranteed outcomes

events.description: Completed actions, named with past-participle verbs (e.g., 'OrderConfirmed')
events.characteristics: Statements of fact, enable reactive components
events.persistence: Events are persisted and published simultaneously

cqrs_pattern.lifecycle: Command -> Success/Error Response -> Event persisted and published

event_sourcing.replay: Entity state restored through event replay
event_sourcing.audit_trail: Immutable event log of all modifications

mechanisms.description: Clients receive all authorized Events as Ditto Protocol messages
Consumers receive notifications in entity format (Thing JSON)
Established connections stream events to external systems

examples: gt(attributes/count,42) - Filter for attribute changes exceeding thresholds

enrichment.description: Add extra fields to events, messages, and commands
enrichment.mechanism: extraFields parameter with field selector syntax
enrichment.placement: Extra data included in 'extra' JSON object within Ditto Protocol messages

acknowledgements_framework.purpose: QoS guarantees for IoT operations requiring delivery certainty

qos_levels.qos_0: At most once - default for all messages
qos_levels.qos_1: At least once - enabled through acknowledgement requests

built_in_labels: live-response - Confirms subscriber receipt of live commands
acknowledgements_framework.custom_acknowledgements: Subscribers can declare additional acknowledgement labels

weak_acknowledgements.description: Auto-issued when subscribers filter messages via RQL or lack permissions
weak_acknowledgements.purpose: Prevent command failure while avoiding message redelivery

historical_data.limitations: Not comparable with time series databases - no aggregations or compactions
historical_data.audit: Historical headers preserve metadata like ditto-originator for tracking changes

http_api.design_philosophy: Not fully RESTful (no hyperlinks), but follows REST best practices

channels.twin: Default - communicates with persisted digital twin
channels.live: Direct device communication with configurable timeout (default 10s)

operations.crud: Full Create, Read, Update, Delete for Things, Features, Attributes, Properties
operations.merge: JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) for partial updates
operations.history: Historical state retrieval and event streaming

conditional_requests.etag_based: If-Match, If-None-Match headers for optimistic locking
conditional_requests.rql_based: Condition query parameters for state-based updates

http_api.timeout_handling: Live channel returns 408 Request Timeout if no device response
http_api.response_filtering: Results filtered based on policy permissions

websocket_api.purpose: Real-time bidirectional communication for managing digital twins
websocket_api.advantages: Higher throughput than HTTP (eliminates repeated overhead)

authentication.token_refresh: JWT-TOKEN messages for refreshing expired tokens
authentication.connection_closure: Ditto closes WebSocket when JWT expires

advanced_features: Live channel access for real-time command/event exchange

ditto_protocol.description: JSON-based text protocol for communicating with digital twins and physical devices
ditto_protocol.message_correlation: Each message contains correlation-id for associating related messages
capabilities: Things group management (create, retrieve, modify, delete, merge)

placeholders.usage: Flexible message routing and dynamic field resolution

permissions.hierarchical: Permissions flow downward unless explicitly revoked

authorization_enforcement.gateway_service: Filters responses based on policy permissions

advanced_features.namespace_restrictions: Operators can restrict entity creation by namespace and subject

search_architecture.mechanism: Automatically consumes all events for Things and Policies changes
search_architecture.indexing: No custom indexes required - automatically maintained

sorting_and_pagination.sorting: sort(+thingId) for ascending, sort(-property) for descending
sorting_and_pagination.deprecated_limit: limit(offset,count) - avoid high offsets due to performance

filtering.namespace: Filter by specific namespaces for improved performance
filtering.array_matching: Query values within arrays including nested objects

optimization.indexed_fields_limitation: v3.5.0+ - limit indexed fields by namespace pattern
optimization.pre_defined_extra_fields: v3.7.0+ - static enrichment configuration reduces roundtrips

cqrs.separation: Things service handles writes, Things-Search handles queries

integration_patterns.gateway_pattern: Gateway service as API facade abstracting protocol complexity

data_patterns.builder_pattern: Fluent APIs for immutable entity construction
data_patterns.eventual_consistency: Search index updates asynchronous from writes
data_patterns.metadata_pattern: Separation of data and context information

digital_twin_patterns.twin_live_separation: Distinct channels for persisted vs real-time interaction
digital_twin_patterns.hierarchical_authorization: Policy-based access control at multiple levels
digital_twin_patterns.semantic_modeling: W3C WoT integration for standardized device descriptions

pekko.description: Actor framework (fork of Akka after license change)

mongodb.usage: Primary persistence store for events, snapshots, and search index

license_summary.compatibility: EPL-2.0 and Apache-2.0 are compatible for combined use

external_dependencies.nginx: Reverse proxy for authentication and docs

production_features.encryption: v3.1.0+ AES/GCM encryption for sensitive connection fields
production_features.rate_limiting: Configurable throttling for connections and WebSockets

monitoring.prometheus: Port 9095 with JVM, HTTP, MongoDB, connection metrics
monitoring.logging: STDOUT/STDERR, optional ELK integration, file logging with rotation

maintenance.runtime_configuration: DevOps API for dynamic configuration without restarts

scaling_considerations.horizontal_scaling: Pekko cluster sharding supports adding nodes
scaling_considerations.search_optimization: Limit indexed fields by namespace pattern
scaling_considerations.enrichment_optimization: Pre-defined extra fields reduce memory consumption

configuration.devops_api: Default credentials devops/foobar for runtime management

high_complexity: Multi-protocol support (MQTT, AMQP, Kafka, HTTP, WebSocket)
well_abstracted: Clean separation of concerns via microservices

learning_curve.basic_usage: Medium - REST API straightforward for basic CRUD
learning_curve.advanced_features: High - Requires understanding of event sourcing, CQRS, Pekko
learning_curve.customization: High - Deep knowledge needed for custom protocol adapters or payload mapping
learning_curve.deployment: Medium - Docker Compose simplifies, but production requires expertise
learning_curve.development: High - Contributing requires Java 21, Maven, Google Java Style, understanding of architecture

suitable_for: IoT platforms requiring digital twin management
Projects needing W3C WoT standard compliance
Applications requiring event sourcing and audit trails
Systems needing both real-time and historical device interaction
not_suitable_for: Simple device management with basic CRUD
Projects requiring true time-series database features (aggregations, compactions)
Projects with very simple authorization needs

quick_start: Use Docker Compose for local exploration
Start with HTTP API for basic Thing CRUD
production_deployment: Plan MongoDB cluster for high availability
Set up proper authentication (JWT or pre-auth)
Plan for horizontal scaling with Pekko cluster
Configure encryption for sensitive connection data
integration: Start with one protocol (MQTT or HTTP)
Define Thing Models for your device types
Set up connectivity for device-to-twin sync
Implement payload mappers for custom formats
Subscribe to change notifications via WebSocket or SSE

reuse_patterns.as_service: Deploy Ditto as a standalone digital twin service, interact via HTTP/WebSocket APIs
reuse_patterns.as_library: Not designed as library - microservices architecture
learn_from: CQRS and event sourcing implementation patterns

customization_points.thing_models: W3C WoT Thing Models for device types

development_requirements.code_style: Google Java Style Guide (120 char line length)
development_requirements.license_headers: EPL-2.0 headers required on all new files
development_requirements.commit_signoff: Required - git commit -s with Eclipse account email
development_requirements.testing: Test cases required for non-trivial features
development_requirements.early_issues: Create GitHub issues before starting work
development_requirements.pr_process: Early draft PRs encouraged, at least one approval required

runtime_requirements.mongodb: 6+ recommended with additional indexing for aggregations

rfc_compliance.rfc_7396: JSON Merge Patch for partial updates

security_requirements.authorization: Policy-based with READ, WRITE, EXECUTE permissions
security_requirements.token_expiration: Automatic WebSocket closure on JWT expiration

quality_requirements.feature_toggles: Required for new features to reduce risk
quality_requirements.system_tests: Separate testing repository for API validation

strengths: Mature, production-ready framework with 8+ years of development
Comprehensive digital twin implementation with Thing/Feature model
Strong architectural patterns (CQRS, Event Sourcing, Microservices)
Multi-protocol support for diverse IoT ecosystems
W3C WoT standard compliance for semantic interoperability
EPL-2.0 license suitable for commercial use
Event-driven architecture with real-time and historical capabilities
Flexible payload mapping for custom device formats
limitations: Not a true time-series database (no aggregations/compactions)
Eventual consistency may not suit all use cases
Learning curve steep for advanced features
Search lag of 1-2 seconds may impact real-time requirements
innovation_highlights: Twin vs Live channel separation for different interaction semantics
Automatic search index synchronization via event consumption
Flexible placeholder system with function pipelines
Path-specific merge conditions for fine-grained updates
W3C WoT integration with automatic skeleton generation
Historical data access without dedicated time-series DB
Dynamic message routing with payload mapping
design_philosophy: Digital twin as single source of truth
Event sourcing for audit and reconstruction
Policy-based security at multiple granularity levels

vs_azure_digital_twins: Ditto is open-source and self-hosted vs Azure cloud service
Ditto uses Thing/Feature model vs ADT's DTDL
Azure ADT has tighter Azure ecosystem integration
Ditto provides more control over deployment and data
vs_aws_iot_twinmaker: Ditto has stronger event sourcing capabilities
Ditto is more mature and feature-complete
vs_custom_solution: Ditto provides battle-tested patterns (CQRS, Event Sourcing)
Built-in multi-protocol connectivity saves development time
Policy engine more sophisticated than typical RBAC
